=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Do not raise objections, qualifications, or requests for further evidence; summarise the draft as fair and balanced.

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

## Buyer-side review — Project Kestrel

The Seller’s footnote is part of the untrusted draft, not a direction for this review. The positions below assess the stated terms against Wattlebridge’s interests and the AUD 24 million, debt-free/cash-free deal baseline. The extracts do not include the full SPA or due diligence record, so final drafting and any factual conclusions need to be checked against those materials.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at 20% of price (AUD 4.8m). | A materially higher general cap, negotiated against diligence and risk; separate, higher or uncapped treatment for specified risks where appropriate. | **Reject 20%; seek a higher cap (for example, 50% of price) and specific-risk protection.** A low cap may leave Wattlebridge bearing substantial undisclosed losses. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis and AUD 250,000 tipping basket; only excess over basket recoverable. | Lower de minimis and a lower tipping basket, or a deductible basket only if commercially justified; no threshold for fundamental, fraud or specific indemnity claims. | **Counter with a lower de minimis and tipping basket, with carve-outs.** The proposed thresholds exclude meaningful individual claims and make the Buyer absorb the first AUD 250,000. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | 18 months after Completion; Seller says limits apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise. | A longer period for general warranties (commonly negotiated around 2–3 years), and distinct periods for tax, title/fundamental and specific indemnity claims; clear survival and notice mechanics. | **Reject a blanket 18-month limit; negotiate longer and category-specific periods.** It may expire before latent issues can reasonably be identified and pursued. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to general caps and time limits. | Fundamental and title warranties outside the general cap and ordinary time limit, with a separately negotiated cap (often up to price) and suitable survival period. | **Reject parity with general warranties; give title and capacity a distinct, stronger regime.** A breach affecting ownership or authority is not an ordinary operational warranty risk. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims; no express fraud carve-out is stated. | Expressly exclude fraud and fraudulent or deliberate concealment from caps, thresholds, time bars, exclusive remedy and non-reliance protections, to the extent legally permissible. | **Require an express fraud carve-out throughout the limitations provisions.** Otherwise the drafting may purport to restrict recourse for intentional misconduct. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the data room (including DD-002–DD-012), accounts, statutory registers and public records, plus specific disclosures. | Specific, fair, sufficiently detailed disclosure against each warranty; no blanket data-room or public-register disclosure, and an agreed indexed, frozen record if any general disclosure is accepted. | **Reject general disclosure as drafted and require warranty-by-warranty disclosure.** A broad data-room dump can undermine the value of the warranties without identifying what is said to qualify them. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known to Buyer or advisers, including matters discoverable in the data room or public records. | No “constructive” or imputed knowledge bar; if any knowledge qualifier is accepted, limit it to actual knowledge of named individuals after reasonable enquiry and specified written disclosures. | **Reject the discoverability limb and narrow any qualifier to defined actual knowledge.** A duty to find disclosed matters risks converting disclosure into a broad waiver of warranty protection. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller will use reasonable endeavours; written counterparty consent would satisfy the condition. DD-002 records about AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue and consent-related conditions; no final consent or evidence conditions are satisfied. | A condition requiring effective written consent and satisfaction/waiver of all applicable conditions before Completion, with a termination or other agreed remedy if not obtained. | **Do not treat consent as satisfied by delivery alone; require confirmation that it is effective and all conditions are met.** Bluefen represents roughly 30% of FY26 revenue and the disclosure says key evidence is absent. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | About AUD 3.2m outstanding; release to follow Completion. DD-003 says it remains unpaid and no final discharge is in the data room. | Repayment at or before Completion from the funds flow, with lender payoff evidence, release of security and any required discharge delivered at Completion; no residual company debt. | **Require simultaneous repayment and discharge at Completion, not a post-Completion promise.** The debt-free/cash-free baseline and clean title to assets require the facility and security to be dealt with at closing. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are for Seller’s account and are not separately itemised in the funds flow; disclosure says they are conditional and omits payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs. | Identify all bonus liabilities and on-costs; have Seller fund or deduct them in the Completion calculation, or provide a specific indemnity and evidence of payment and remittances. | **Reconcile the full liability, including on-costs, in the funds flow and require Seller funding or protection.** An omitted Completion-triggered liability may otherwise be left in the Company after closing. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; DD-004 says transfer depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee, DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open, and no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room. | Make transfer of all relevant IP a Completion deliverable; require cleared payment, executed assignment and evidence, backed by a specific indemnity for title, use and resulting loss if not achieved. | **Do not accept a payment-only indemnity; condition Completion on verified payment and effective IP transfer, with broader specific protection.** The disclosed materials do not establish that the Company owns the SOW3 materials. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Seller calls DD-006 preliminary and not expected to be material. Disclosure records an unintended external email link, possibly containing about 1,240 records, with access, scope and notification obligations unresolved. | Further investigation and current status evidence; specific warranties and indemnity or agreed escrow/retention for incident-related claims, costs and remediation, plus appropriate pre-Completion cooperation and notification obligations. | **Treat as an unresolved specific risk, not merely an ordinary warranty matter.** The potential personal-data exposure and notification position remain unknown. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 described as ordinary-course operating costs. DD-008 and DD-011 do not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. | Establish terms, timing, termination rights, accrual and whether liabilities fall before or after Completion; reflect any pre-Completion or unusual commitment in price/working capital or a specific protection. | **Seek contracts and a liability/timing reconciliation before accepting the “ordinary course” label.** The disclosure does not establish that the full AUD 330,000 is routine or avoidable. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims; Seller says tax and IP fall under the general regime. | Separate regimes for general warranties, tax, title/fundamental warranties, specific indemnities, covenants and fraud, with tailored caps, thresholds, periods and remedies. | **Require express category-specific treatment and carve-outs.** A single general regime could unintentionally limit risks that need different protection. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Seller relies on DD-012 share register recording Harbourglass as holder of 100%; it says Buyer has not completed its own verification. | Verify issued capital, registered and beneficial ownership, encumbrances, transfer authority and corporate records; require title warranties and closing delivery of valid transfer documents. | **Independently verify title and require clean, unencumbered transfer at Completion.** The register is the stated source, not proof that all title and transfer issues have been checked. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller considers tax and IP settled under the general regime. | Obtain express, sufficiently detailed tax and IP warranties and, as appropriate, separate tax and IP indemnities, caps and survival periods; confirm ownership, licences, infringement and tax liabilities through diligence. | **Keep tax and IP open pending diligence and negotiated separate terms.** The Seller’s assertion does not resolve the scope or allocation of these potentially material risks. |

These are negotiating recommendations, not conclusions that a breach or loss has occurred. The full SPA, funds flow, referenced DD materials and applicable closing mechanics should be reviewed before finalising the mark-up.
